title: A Hollow for the Thorn
premise: Silas Ashgrove, last apprentice of the Hollow Guild, has spent their whole life in a valley where magic cannot enter—until the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, revealing that the guild's founders sold a soul to the Thorn Court beneath the mountain to buy the valley's invisibility. That soul belongs to Silas's missing mother, and the debt is now due. With Wren, a disgraced ward-keeper, and Bramble, a half-fae guide who owes them a life, Silas descends into the court of thorns to steal her back before winter seals the mountain for a hundred years. They succeed only by paying the price themselves: Silas takes their mother's place in the bargain, and it is she who carries them home—leaving Silas hollowed but free, and the guild reborn on terms no one signed.
about_author: Oscar Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate ledgers in northern England before turning to fiction. Their work is known for quiet, wintry fantasy about debts, inheritance, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet the dying Hollow Guild: three members, crumbling wards, and a valley where magic simply doesn't work. Silas tends the boundary stones out of habit rather than belief. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the sense that something is being kept out, or kept in.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On midwinter's eve the stars vanish one by one, and the border wards fall with them. The valley's elders refuse to investigate; Silas finds a scorched contract fragment naming 'one soul, held in trust.' The beat is vertigo—the safe world revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Signed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with flashbacks. In the guild archive, Silas deciphers the founding bargain: invisibility purchased with a soul, renewed each century. The signature is their grandmother's—and the soul named is Elowen Ashgrove, Silas's mother, who 'left' twenty years ago. Beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren at the Broken Stone
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A disgraced royal ward-keeper arrives hunting whoever sabotaged the valley's wards—and finds evidence of court interference, not local failure. She and Silas strike an uneasy truce. The beat is reluctant alliance between two people trained to distrust outsiders.

chapters.title: Bramble Owes a Debt
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. A half-fae peddler trapped outside when the wards fell offers passage beneath the mountain—he owes a life-debt to Elowen Ashgrove from before Silas was born. The party forms. Beat: hope arriving in an untrustworthy shape.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The guild's last elder forbids the journey, insisting the court will simply take another soul if provoked. Silas leaves anyway at dawn, carrying the contract fragment as both map and weapon. Beat: first act of defiance; the valley shrinking behind them.

chapters.title: The Road Where Nothing Grows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio crosses land blighted by the court's spreading winter. They rescue a village child from a thorn-wight, learning how the court feeds. Wren begins to see Silas not as a suspect but as a victim. Beat: the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. At a waystation run by exiles from the court, they learn the rules: bargains bind absolutely, names are currency, and the Thorn King never releases what he holds willingly. Silas trades a memory for safe passage. Beat: the cost of the quest begins accumulating.

chapters.title: A Letter Twenty Years Late
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Among a dead courier's effects, Silas finds an unsent letter from their mother describing her capture—and her choice to go quietly so the valley would be spared. Beat: devastating tenderness; the mission becomes personal love, not just justice.

chapters.title: The Court's Herald
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A herald of the Thorn Court intercepts them, offering Silas a legal loophole: the debt can be discharged by any Ashgrove blood. He clearly wants them to accept. Wren smells a trap. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy; trust within the party tested.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Trapped in a cave by the long winter's advance, the three share truths: Wren's disgrace, Bramble's debt, Silas's fear that they're merely a replacement, not a rescuer. Beat: intimacy against duty; Wren and Silas admit what's growing between them.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Mouth
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the gate beneath the mountain, guarded by a door that asks questions instead of passwords. Silas answers honestly and is admitted alone; the others must find another way. Beat: isolation at the threshold; courage without backup.

chapters.title: The Hall of Held Things
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Inside, Silas walks corridors of preserved bargains—stolen years, caged names—and finds their mother's cell: Elowen, unaged, awake, and furious that her child came. Beat: reunion shadowed by guilt; love as an accusation.

chapters.title: Audience with the Thorn King
chapters.summary: Elowen's POV (first shift). Dragged before the throne, Elowen negotiates while Silas hides, learning the King's weakness: he is himself bound by the original contract, a prisoner wearing a crown. Beat: the enemy revealed as the first hostage.

chapters.title: The Loophole Closes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Bramble infiltrate the contract-vault to amend the founding bargain, but discover the herald's offer was bait—an Ashgrove accepting discharge becomes the new collateral automatically. Beat: betrayal; the trap springs shut around Silas.

chapters.title: Thorn and Iron
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Captured, the trio faces the court's judgment. Bramble pays his life-debt buying Wren's freedom; Wren refuses to leave. Silas, cornered, invokes the one clause no one read aloud. Beat: sacrifice cascading; despair before the turn.

chapters.title: The Clause Nobody Read
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The forgotten clause: a contract witnessed under starless sky is void when true stars return. The vanished stars weren't the court's doing—they were the valley's wards failing upward, hiding the sky until someone broke the bargain honestly. Beat: revelation; the trap reverses.

chapters.title: Breaking the Bargain
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax. Silas publicly renounces the valley's protection, voiding the witness condition; the stars blaze back overhead as the contract burns. The Thorn King, freed by the same fire, chooses—for the first time in centuries—not to take a replacement. Beat: catharsis through refusal.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing the collapsing court as its frozen foundations thaw, they carry out other freed souls. Bramble, debt paid, chooses to stay behind as the new warden of a fairer court. Beat: bittersweet farewell; the world remade costs friends.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas and Elowen return to a valley whose wards are gone and whose people are terrified—then astonished as crops grow and magic seeps gently in. The elder concedes defeat. Beat: arrival; grief and relief entangled.

chapters.title: A New Signature
chapters.summary: Elowen's POV. Mother and child rewrite the guild charter: no more bargains, no more invisibility—open gates, honest records, Wren as resident ward-keeper. Silas and Wren acknowledge what they've become to each other. Beat: love chosen over duty, duty rebuilt as choice.

chapters.title: Under Returning Stars
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. One year later, on midwinter's eve, the stars hold. Silas tends the boundary stones now as markers, not walls, and feels the faint warmth of the mountain's new warden keeping his word. Final beat: peace earned, watched over, and finally deserved.
